aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

aceldama.title: Aceldama
aceldama.note: Aramaic for field of blood, and the name stuck to the plot bought with the money Judas took for handing over Jesus.

aeneas.title: Aeneas
aeneas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
aeneas.note: Paralysed and in bed for eight years at Lydda until Peter told him to get up and make his bed. Many in Lydda and on the plain of Sharon turned to the Lord after it.

alexander-3.title: Alexander
alexander-3.about: Priest living at the time of the New Testament
alexander-3.note: One of 4 men called Alexander. This one is a priest from the New Testament, named once in Acts.

alpheus.title: Alpheus
alpheus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
alpheus.note: Father of the apostle James, which is how that James is told apart from James the son of Zebedee.

ananias.title: Ananias
ananias.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
ananias.note: He was the disciple in Damascus who restored Paul's sight and baptised him. He was afraid of the man who had been persecuting Christians, and he went anyway.

ananias-2.title: Ananias
ananias-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
ananias-2.note: He and his wife Sapphira sold land and brought the apostles part of the money as if it were all of it. Peter told him he had lied to God and not to people, and he dropped dead on the spot. Sapphira told the same lie a few hours later and died the same way.

andrew.title: Andrew
andrew.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
andrew.note: Peter's brother, and in John's Gospel a disciple of John the Baptist first, who followed Jesus and straight away brought Peter to meet him. He keeps turning up at practical moments: the boy with five loaves and two fish, the Greeks who came asking for Jesus. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross.

annas.title: Annas
annas.about: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
annas.note: High priest from AD 6 to 15, put in by the Roman legate Quirinius and removed by the procurator Valerius Gratus. Rome could take the office off him and apparently not the standing: the Gospels still call him high priest next to Caiaphas, who was his son-in-law.

arabian.title: Arabian
arabian.note: Desert peoples from south and east of Israel. They brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and in Jehoram's reign they helped the Philistines raid Judah.

asia.title: Asia
asia.note: Not the continent. The Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus among its churches, and the region the seven churches of Revelation belonged to.

azotus.title: Azotus
azotus.note: Ashdod's Greek name, and where Philip the evangelist turned up after he baptized the Ethiopian official, carrying on along the coastal road.

babylon.title: Babylon
babylon.note: The Mesopotamian empire that destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off. Later Scripture, Revelation included, uses its name as shorthand for worldly power.

barnabas.title: Barnabas
barnabas.about: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
barnabas.note: Joseph was his given name. He was a Levite from Cyprus. The apostles called him Barnabas, son of encouragement, after he sold a field and gave the money to the Jerusalem church.

barsabas.title: Barsabas
barsabas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
barsabas.note: Son of Sabas, a surname two men carry in Acts. This one is Joseph, also called Justus, one of the two put forward to take Judas's place among the twelve.

bartholomeus.title: Bartholomeus
bartholomeus.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
bartholomeus.note: One of the twelve. Many take him for Nathanael, since the Synoptic Gospels never mention a Nathanael and John's Gospel never mentions a Bartholomew.

caesarea.title: Caesarea
caesarea.note: Herod the Great built it as a Roman port on the Mediterranean coast, and it served as the administrative capital of Roman Judea. Cornelius the centurion lived there. Paul spent two years there in prison.

caiaphas.title: Caiaphas
caiaphas.about: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
caiaphas.note: The high priest who presided over the council that condemned Jesus. Beforehand he argued it was better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to suffer, and John's Gospel reads those words as more than he knew.

candace.title: Candace
candace.note: A title the ruling queens of Kush carried, the way Egypt's kings were all Pharaoh. The official Philip met served one of them.

cappadocia.title: Cappadocia
cappadocia.note: A large province in eastern Asia Minor. Jews from there were in Jerusalem at Pentecost, and later Peter wrote to the scattered believers there among others.

chanaan.title: Chanaan
chanaan.note: The King James spelling of Canaan in Acts, where Stephen's speech looks back on the land promised to Abraham's descendants.

charran.title: Charran
charran.note: Haran, in the Greek form Stephen uses before the Sanhedrin. Abraham settled there with his father Terah after leaving Ur, and moved on to Canaan once Terah had died.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

cilicia.title: Cilicia
cilicia.note: Paul was born in Tarsus, Cilicia's chief city, on the southeastern coast of Asia Minor. Cilician Jews had their own synagogue in Jerusalem and argued with Stephen there. The province was known for the goat's hair cloth used in tentmaking, which was Paul's trade.

cornelius.title: Cornelius
cornelius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
cornelius.note: A Roman centurion at Caesarea, devout, generous, and not a Jew. An angel told him to send for Peter while a vision got Peter ready to come. When the Holy Spirit fell on his household as it had at Pentecost, the Jerusalem church accepted that Gentiles did not have to become Jews first.

cretan.title: Cretan
cretan.note: People of Crete, the big island where Paul left Titus to set the churches in order and appoint elders.

cyrene.title: Cyrene
cyrene.note: Greek colonists founded it in North Africa around 630 BC, and its temple of Apollo and theatre still stand near Shahhat in Libya. Simon of Cyrene carried Jesus's cross. Cyrenian believers helped start the mixed church at Antioch, and Lucius of Cyrene taught there.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

dorcas.title: Dorcas
dorcas.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
dorcas.note: Tabitha in Aramaic, a woman at Joppa who made clothes for the widows. When she died the disciples sent for Peter and he raised her, and many in Joppa believed because of it.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

egyptian.title: Egyptian
egyptian.note: In Acts a Roman officer takes Paul for the Egyptian, a rebel who had recently led an armed rising. Josephus mentions the same man.

elamite.title: Elamite
elamite.note: People from Elam, the old civilisation centred on Susa in what is now southwestern Iran. Ezra has them among those resettled in Samaria who opposed rebuilding Jerusalem, and Acts puts them in the Pentecost crowd.

emmor.title: Emmor
emmor.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
emmor.note: Hamor, in Greek. Stephen names him as the man Abraham bought a tomb from, where Genesis gives that purchase to Jacob, and many read it as Stephen folding two land purchases into one.

ethiopian.title: Ethiopian
ethiopian.note: The Candace's treasurer, a eunuch, reading Isaiah in his chariot on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza. Philip told him the passage was about Jesus and baptised him there and then.

galilee.title: Galilee
galilee.note: Jesus grew up here and did most of his public work around the Sea of Galilee. Judeans thought the north provincial and mixed, which is the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.

gamaliel-2.title: Gamaliel
gamaliel-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
gamaliel-2.note: Acts names him twice, and he is a man from the New Testament.

gaza.title: Gaza
gaza.note: Samson pulled down the temple of Dagon here, and Philip met the Ethiopian official on the desert road toward it. It was one of the five Philistine cities, assigned to Judah and never fully held, and Egyptian records already name it in the second millennium BC.

grecian.title: Grecian
grecian.note: Greek-speaking Jews, as against Hebrew-speaking ones. They complained that their widows were losing out in the daily food, and that is how Stephen and six others came to be appointed.

hebrew-2.title: Hebrew
hebrew-2.note: In the New Testament it can mean the Jewish people, their old language or their traditional way of life. Philippians 3:5 has a Hebrew born of Hebrews.

herod.title: Herod
herod.about: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
herod.note: Herod Antipas, the son of Herod the Great. He ruled Galilee through Jesus's ministry and beheaded John the Baptist for condemning his marriage, and Luke has him mock Jesus before the crucifixion.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

israelite.title: Israelite
israelite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israelite.note: One of the people descended from Jacob, who was renamed Israel. Paul calls himself an Israelite in Romans 11 when he argues God has not dropped his people.

italian.title: Italian
italian.note: In Acts 10 Cornelius is a centurion of the Italian Cohort at Caesarea, a Roman auxiliary unit. Inscriptions from Syria show a Cohors II Italica in the region in the first century, and many scholars take it to be this unit.

jacob-2.title: Jacob
jacob-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob-2.note: In the New Testament the name mostly means the patriarch, set beside Abraham and Isaac, and Luke's angel promises Mary that Jesus will reign "over the house of Jacob forever". Matthew's genealogy also has a Jacob as the father of Joseph.

james-4.title: James
james-4.about: Father of an apostle living at the time of the New Testament
james-4.note: A man from the New Testament, named twice across Luke and Acts.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

joel-4.title: Joel
joel-4.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joel-4.note: A prophet from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across Joel and Acts.

john-2.title: John
john-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
john-2.note: Zebedee's son and James's younger brother, a fisherman, and with Peter and James one of the three who saw what the rest did not, the transfiguration and Gethsemane among it. From the cross Jesus gave him his mother Mary to look after. Tradition makes him the disciple Jesus loved and credits him with the fourth Gospel, three letters, and Revelation, written in exile on Patmos.

john-4.title: John
john-4.about: Priest living at the time of the New Testament
john-4.note: A priest from the New Testament, and Acts is the only book that names him.

john.title: John
john.about: Prophet living at the time of the New Testament
john.note: The prophet who comes out of the wilderness in Matthew 3, preaching repentance and baptising. Jesus came to him to be baptised. Later, from prison, he sent his own disciples to ask whether Jesus was the one.

joppa.title: Joppa
joppa.note: Judea's main seaport, a point of land on the Mediterranean. Jonah sailed from there running from Nineveh, and cedar for Solomon's and Zerubbabel's temples came ashore there. In Acts, Peter raised Tabitha at Joppa and, staying with Simon the tanner, had the vision that opened the gospel to Gentiles.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

joseph-5.title: Joseph
joseph-5.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
joseph-5.note: A man from the New Testament. Acts names him once.

joseph-2.title: Joseph
joseph-2.about: Mary's husband living at the time of the New Testament
joseph-2.note: A descendant of David from Nazareth, engaged to Mary when she turned out to be pregnant. An angel in a dream talked him out of quietly ending it, and he raised Jesus as his legal father. Scripture says nothing of him after Jesus's boyhood.

judaea.title: Judaea
judaea.note: The Roman name for the southern part of the land around Jerusalem, roughly old Judah. Client kings of Herod's family ruled it, then Roman procurators like Pontius Pilate. John the Baptist preached in its wilderness and the Passion happened there. After the revolt of AD 66 to 70 Rome struck coins reading "Judaea Capta."

justus.title: Justus
justus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
justus.note: A second name several early Christians carried. One was a man in Corinth whose house stood next door to the synagogue, and Paul used it as a meeting place.

levite.title: Levite
levite.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
levite.note: They belonged to the tribe of Levi and served at the tabernacle and later the temple, helping the priests, who came from Aaron's branch of the same tribe. Their work was religious, so they got no tribal land, only forty eight towns among the other tribes and the tithes of Israel. Over time they carried and guarded the holy things, sang, kept the gates, and taught the law.

libertine.title: Libertine
libertine.about: Group of Jews in the New Testament
libertine.note: Members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen in Jerusalem, Jews once enslaved in Rome and later set free, possibly taken there after Pompey conquered Judea in 63 BC. Some of them argued with Stephen and helped bring the false charges that got him killed.

libya.title: Libya
libya.note: North Africa west of Egypt, with Cyrene its main city in the Greco-Roman period. People from Libya were in Jerusalem at Pentecost.

lydda.title: Lydda
lydda.note: About nine miles southeast of Joppa on the coastal plain. Peter healed a paralysed man named Aeneas there, and many in the plain of Sharon turned to the Lord. Today it is Lod, where Ben Gurion Airport is.

madian.title: Madian
madian.note: Midian, in Greek. Moses ran there after killing an Egyptian and kept sheep for his father-in-law until God called him at the burning bush.

mary.title: Mary
mary.about: Jesus' mother living at the time of the New Testament
mary.note: Jesus' mother. She was engaged to Joseph when Gabriel told her she would bear the Messiah, she raised Jesus in Nazareth, and she stood at the cross when he died.

matthew.title: Matthew
matthew.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
matthew.note: A tax collector, which made him an outcast among fellow Jews for working on Rome's behalf, until Jesus called him straight from his booth to be one of the twelve. Mark and Luke call him Levi. He threw a big dinner for Jesus with other tax collectors, and early church tradition says he wrote the Gospel that carries his name, aimed at Jewish readers.

matthias.title: Matthias
matthias.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
matthias.note: The eleven drew lots between two men who had been with Jesus since his baptism, and the lot fell on Matthias, to take Judas Iscariot's place before Pentecost. The New Testament says nothing more about him.

mede.title: Mede
mede.note: Someone from Media, an old kingdom in what is now northwestern Iran. The Medes joined Babylon to bring down Assyria, then merged with Persia under Cyrus. Daniel talks about their laws and kings, and Medes were in the Pentecost crowd in Acts 2:9.

mesopotamia.title: Mesopotamia
mesopotamia.note: The land between the rivers, the Euphrates and the Tigris, which the Old Testament calls Aram-naharaim or Padan-aram. Abraham's family came from there, as Stephen reminds the Sanhedrin, and pilgrims from there were in Jerusalem at Pentecost. Clay archives from Mari and Nuzi in the same region show customs of adoption, inheritance and marriage much like the ones in Genesis.

moloch.title: Moloch
moloch.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
moloch.note: The Ammonite god, worshipped by burning children, and the same as Molech, Milcom and Malcham. Solomon built him a high place on the Mount of Olives for his foreign wives, and Josiah tore it down. Stephen quotes Amos against his worship in front of the Sanhedrin.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

nazarene.title: Nazarene
nazarene.note: It means from Nazareth, Jesus' home town, and it became the name for his followers too, "the sect of the Nazarenes" in Acts 24:5. Matthew ties it to prophecy, possibly playing on the Hebrew word for "branch" in Isaiah 11. Arabic and Hebrew still call Christians by it.

nazareth.title: Nazareth
nazareth.note: A small village in the hills of Galilee, never named in the Old Testament and not thought much of, which is likely the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come from it. Gabriel came to Mary there, and Jesus grew up there. When he preached in its synagogue, his neighbours drove him out.

nicanor.title: Nicanor
nicanor.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
nicanor.note: The Jerusalem church picked seven men to run the daily food for widows after the Hellenistic and Hebrew believers fell out, and Nicanor was one of them. That is all the New Testament says.

nicolaus.title: Nicolaus
nicolaus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
nicolaus.note: One of the seven the Jerusalem church picked to oversee the daily food for widows, and called a proselyte of Antioch, a Gentile who had converted to Judaism before he came to Christ.

olivet.title: Olivet
olivet.note: The ridge east of Jerusalem. Jesus taught his disciples there about what was coming, and he wept over the city from it. Gethsemane sits at its foot, and Luke and Acts put the ascension here too.

pamphylia.title: Pamphylia
pamphylia.note: Jews from Pamphylia were in Jerusalem at Pentecost. The province lay on the south coast of Asia Minor between Lycia and Cilicia. Paul and Barnabas came ashore at its capital, Perga.

parmenas.title: Parmenas
parmenas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
parmenas.note: Another of the seven picked by the Jerusalem church to oversee the daily food for widows, so the apostles could keep to prayer and preaching (Acts 6:5).

parthian.title: Parthian
parthian.note: At Pentecost the crowd in Jerusalem is listed nation by nation, and Parthians come first. These were Jews of the dispersion from the Parthian empire, Rome's great rival in the east, centered on Persia and Mesopotamia.

paul-2.title: Paul
paul-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
paul-2.note: A man from the New Testament. Acts names him 5 times.

pentecost.title: Pentecost
pentecost.note: The harvest festival fifty days after Passover. It is the day the Spirit came down on the disciples in Jerusalem. Peter preached, and that is where the church starts.

peter.title: Peter
peter.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
peter.note: A Galilean fisherman named Simon. Jesus renamed him Cephas, or Peter, which means rock. He became the most prominent of the twelve, and in Matthew it is his confession that Jesus is the Messiah the Gospel turns on.

pharaoh-2.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-2.note: Joseph's Pharaoh. Potiphar was his officer, his baker and butler landed in prison with Joseph, and his dreams of fat and thin cows were what got Joseph out and set him over Egypt.

pharaoh-4.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-4.note: The Pharaoh who put Israel to forced labour on store cities. He then ordered the Hebrew baby boys thrown into the river. His own daughter pulled one of them out.

pharisee.title: Pharisee
pharisee.about: Religious group in the New Testament
pharisee.note: A Jewish movement devoted to strict keeping of the law, the written text and a large body of oral tradition around it. They carried real weight in the religious life of the people. They argue with Jesus again and again.

philip.title: Philip
philip.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
philip.note: One of the twelve, from Bethsaida like Peter and Andrew. Philip found Nathanael and brought him to Jesus, and in John's Gospel he gets asked how they were going to feed the crowd.

philip-2.title: Philip
philip-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
philip-2.note: Not the apostle. This Philip was one of the seven chosen to oversee the food in the Jerusalem church. He became a traveling evangelist and led the Ethiopian eunuch to faith.

phrygia.title: Phrygia
phrygia.note: A big inland region of Asia Minor, with Colossae, Hierapolis, Laodicea and Iconium among its cities. Jews from Phrygia heard the apostles at Pentecost. Paul went through the region more than once.

pilate.title: Pilate
pilate.about: Ruler living at the time of the New Testament
pilate.note: Pontius Pilate, Roman governor of Judea. He said three times that he found no guilt in Jesus, and then gave the crowd and the religious leaders what they wanted and had him crucified.

pontius.title: Pontius
pontius.about: Ruler living at the time of the New Testament
pontius.note: Pilate's family name, and the reader wants the entry for Pilate.

pontus.title: Pontus
pontus.note: A Roman province along the southern coast of the Black Sea. Jews from Pontus were at Pentecost in Jerusalem, and Peter wrote his first letter partly to believers scattered there.

prochorus.title: Prochorus
prochorus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
prochorus.note: Named third among the seven picked to oversee the daily food for widows, right after Stephen and Philip.

remphan.title: Remphan
remphan.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
remphan.note: A star god, not a man. Stephen, quoting Amos, said Israel carried his image in the wilderness. The name is likely another for Saturn, or for the god called Chiun.

sadducee.title: Sadducee
sadducee.about: Religious group in the New Testament
sadducee.note: A party drawn mostly from the priestly aristocracy. They rejected the oral tradition the Pharisees kept, and they denied the resurrection of the body.

samaria.title: Samaria
samaria.note: Omri bought a hill from a man called Shemer and built a capital on it. Samaria took over from Tirzah as the seat of the northern kingdom. Ahab and the kings after him ruled from there.

samaritan.title: Samaritan
samaritan.note: The people who lived in Samaria in Jesus' day. 2 Kings traces them back to the Israelites left behind and the foreigners Assyria brought in. They worshiped at a temple of their own.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

sapphira.title: Sapphira
sapphira.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
sapphira.note: She and her husband Ananias sold property and lied to the apostles about how much they were giving. Peter put the same question to her that he had put to him, and she did not know Ananias was already dead.

saron.title: Saron
saron.note: Sharon, in its Greek form. Acts 9:35 says the people of Lydda and Saron turned to the Lord when they saw the paralyzed man healed. It is the coastal plain between Joppa and Mount Carmel.

satan.title: Satan
satan.about: An angel in the Old Testament
satan.note: The name means adversary. In Job he questions whether Job's goodness is real, and in Zechariah he stands to accuse Joshua the high priest before the angel of the Lord.

saul-2.title: Saul
saul-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
saul-2.note: Paul's name before the road to Damascus. Acts keeps calling him Saul for some time after he turned, and the rest of his story is under Paul.

simon-4.title: Simon
simon-4.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
simon-4.note: One of the twelve apostles. The title Zealot tells him apart from Simon Peter and probably means he had belonged to a movement opposed to Roman rule. Nothing else about him is recorded.

simon.title: Simon
simon.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simon.note: Simon Peter, called from his fishing in Matthew 4:18 and named first among the twelve apostles. In Matthew 16:16 he is the one who answers the question.

simon-2.title: Simon
simon-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simon-2.note: A tanner whose house was by the sea. Peter lodged with him, and the messengers in Acts 10:17 came to his gate asking for Peter.

simon-3.title: Simon
simon-3.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simon-3.note: He practised magic and had the people amazed, until he believed and was baptized himself. Then he offered the apostles money for their power, and Peter told him his money could perish with him.

sina.title: Sina
sina.note: Sinai, in its Greek form. Stephen uses it when he tells of God appearing to Moses at the mountain. Paul turns Mount Sinai into an allegory in Galatians.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

stephen.title: Stephen
stephen.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
stephen.note: He was picked as one of seven to oversee the food for the Greek-speaking widows in the Jerusalem church. He soon became known for miracles and bold debate instead.

sychem.title: Sychem
sychem.note: Stephen's Greek spelling of Shechem, in the speech he gave before the Sanhedrin. He says the patriarchs were buried in a tomb Abraham bought there from the sons of Hamor, though Genesis records two separate purchases, Machpelah at Hebron and Jacob's land at Shechem.

tabitha.title: Tabitha
tabitha.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
tabitha.note: A disciple at Joppa, known for doing good and giving to the poor. She died, the believers sent for Peter, and he raised her. Luke gives both her Aramaic name and the Greek one, Dorcas, and both mean gazelle.

tarsus.title: Tarsus
tarsus.note: Paul was born here, in the capital of Cilicia on the Cydnus River, about twelve miles from the sea, and he called it no mean city. It had schools of philosophy and rhetoric that rivalled Athens and Alexandria.

theophilus.title: Theophilus
theophilus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
theophilus.note: Luke wrote both his Gospel and Acts to him. He calls him most excellent, the title he also uses for Felix and Festus, and that is all anyone knows.

theudas.title: Theudas
theudas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
theudas.note: Gamaliel's example of a movement that died with its leader. Theudas raised a following, he was killed, and it came to nothing. Josephus mentions a rebel Theudas around AD 44, later than Gamaliel's speech, and whether that is the same man has never been settled.

thomas.title: Thomas
thomas.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
thomas.note: One of the twelve, called the twin. He would not believe Jesus had risen until he could touch the wounds, and when Jesus showed him his hands and side he said, my Lord and my God.

timon.title: Timon
timon.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
timon.note: One of the seven chosen to handle the daily food for widows in the Jerusalem church. Nothing more is known of him.

zelotes.title: Zelotes
zelotes.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
zelotes.note: The Zealot, Luke's way of telling Simon the apostle from Simon Peter, and Matthew and Mark call him Simon the Canaanite, which means the same thing.
